newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Senate passes shipping bill.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Senate passes shipping bill.

text.p: The key Independent members of the Australian Senate on Friday sided with the government on second bill for the day, ensuring unamended passage of a measure to end government subsidies of seafarer's wages.
The Shipping Grants Legislation Bill, a minor element of the Australian budget, aimed to save about A$20 million a year from July 1997 by ending the subsidies.
The subsidies, a policy of the former Labor government, effectively exempted seafarers from income tax.
Earlier the Independents, Brian Harradine and Mal Colston, backed a bill that redirected schools funding.
The Labor Opposition and the Australian Democrats and Greens minor parties all opposed the shipping measure.
But the government needs only two extra votes to get legislation through the upper house of parliament, and Independents Brian Harradine and Mal Colston for the second time on Friday supplied them.
The government expects to depend on Harradine and Colston for some of the contentious budget-cutting measures that will come before the Senate over the coming two weeks.
Those contentious measures are worth more than A$1 billion a year to the budget.
